listening-text-1.transcript:
W: Hello, can I pay by credit card for the pizza?
M: I'm sorry, our restaurant is not set up to take credit cards over the phone for delivery orders. It's cash only, and we would appreciate it if you paid our driver with the smallest bill possible.
listening-text-1.translationZh:
女：你好，我订的披萨能用信用卡付款吗？
男：抱歉，我们餐厅不支持外卖订单在电话里用信用卡付款。只收现金，另外您付钱给送餐司机时，如果能尽量用小面额的钞票，我们会很感激。
listening-text-1.summaryZh: 女士打电话订披萨外卖，询问能否用信用卡付款，店员说明了付款规定。

sentences.zh: 你好，我订的披萨能用信用卡付款吗？

listening-text-2.transcript:
M: So, as an expert, what new technology do you think we will see in 2026?
W: We will continue to see improvements in machine learning and computer intelligence, leading to progress in the Internet of Things and 6G. I also hope to see new clean energy technology coming into the market.
listening-text-2.translationZh:
男：那么，作为专家，您认为 2026 年我们会看到哪些新技术？
女：机器学习和计算机智能会继续进步，从而推动物联网和 6G 的发展。我也希望看到新的清洁能源技术进入市场。
listening-text-2.summaryZh: 男士与一位女专家交谈，话题是 2026 年可能出现的新技术。

sentences.zh: 那么，作为专家，您认为 2026 年我们会看到哪些新技术？

listening-text-3.transcript:
W: I have heard you are going to England tomorrow. I want to see you off at the airport. When will you leave?
M: One in the afternoon. But I am to check in at 11:20 in the morning.
W: Then I will see you at the airport at 11 in the morning.
listening-text-3.translationZh:
女：听说你明天要去英国。我想去机场送你。你什么时候走？
男：下午一点。不过我上午十一点二十就得办理登机手续。
女：那我上午十一点在机场跟你碰面。
listening-text-3.summaryZh: 男士明天要去英国，女士打算去机场送行，两人商量在机场见面的时间。

listening-text-4.transcript:
W: Have you ever watched the game for disabled athletes?
M: Yes, watching these athletes is a moving experience.
W: Because disabled athletes have to adapt to their disability and make a huge effort to succeed. So they need encouragement and shouldn't be made fun of.
M: I couldn't agree more.
listening-text-4.translationZh:
女：你看过残疾人运动会吗？
男：看过，看这些运动员比赛让人很感动。
女：因为残疾运动员得适应自己的残疾，还要付出巨大的努力才能成功。所以他们需要鼓励，不应该被人取笑。
男：我完全同意。
listening-text-4.summaryZh: 一男一女谈起观看残疾人运动会的感受，交流对残疾运动员的看法。

listening-text-5.transcript:
W: Most of the world's rainforests are in danger. They are disappearing at an alarming rate.
M: Yeah, many plants and a large population of animals exist only in rainforest. Have you heard of the Amazon rainforest fires in 2019?
W: Yes, they led to mass loss of wildlife.
listening-text-5.translationZh:
女：世界上大部分雨林都处于危险之中，正以惊人的速度消失。
男：是啊，很多植物和大量动物只生活在雨林里。你听说过 2019 年亚马孙雨林大火吗？
女：听说过，那场大火造成大量野生动物死亡。
listening-text-5.summaryZh: 一男一女聊起世界雨林的现状，还说到 2019 年的亚马孙雨林大火。

listening-text-6.transcript:
M: Globe Language Center. May I help you?
W: Yes, I'd like some information about your study abroad programs.
M: Sure. Our short-term programs are eight weeks long.
W: Eight weeks is perfect. I have to start a new job in the fall. Can you tell me what kind of housing is out there?
M: We place all of our students in homestay. If you like, I can send you our brochure and some information about our host families.
W: Okay, thanks.
listening-text-6.translationZh:
男：环球语言中心，有什么可以帮您？
女：是的，我想了解一下你们的留学项目。
男：好的。我们的短期项目为期八周。
女：八周正合适。我秋天得开始一份新工作。你能说说那边的住宿是什么样的吗？
男：我们把所有学生都安排在寄宿家庭。如果您愿意，我可以把我们的宣传册和一些寄宿家庭的资料寄给您。
女：好的，谢谢。
listening-text-6.summaryZh: 女士打电话向一家语言中心咨询留学短期项目和住宿安排。

listening-text-7.transcript:
W: You don't look well. What troubles you, Daniel?
M: Well, you know, our music teacher has asked me to prepare something for the city piano competition. I have chosen a piece of Beethoven's music.
W: That is great, Daniel. We all know you are the best in our class, and I hope you will win.
M: The only problem is that my mother is not feeling well. Can you imagine what my practicing at home would do to her?
W: There must be a solution.
listening-text-7.translationZh:
女：你脸色不太好。有什么烦心事吗，丹尼尔？
男：嗯，你知道，我们的音乐老师让我为全市钢琴比赛准备一首曲子。我选了一首贝多芬的作品。
女：太好了，丹尼尔。大家都知道你是我们班最棒的，我希望你能赢。
男：唯一的问题是我妈妈身体不舒服。你能想象我在家练琴会对她有什么影响吗？
女：总会有办法的。
listening-text-7.summaryZh: 丹尼尔要准备全市钢琴比赛，他向关心他的女孩说起自己的烦恼。

listening-text-8.transcript:
M: Hi, Elena. Congratulations on bringing out your book about fundraising for nonprofit organizations.
W: Thanks. I couldn't have done it without the support from everyone here at the Society for Wildlife Preservation.
M: If it is possible, I would like you to give a talk on your book to the public. I think it would really encourage everyone to think creatively about how we can attract more donors to help our cause.
W: Sure, I can do that, but it will have to wait until next month because I am going to a meeting on protecting the wetlands.

男：你好，埃琳娜。祝贺你出版了那本讲如何为非营利组织筹款的书。
女：谢谢。没有野生动物保护协会这里每个人的支持，我不可能做到。
男：如果可以的话，我想请你就这本书给公众做一次讲座。我觉得这真的会鼓励大家创造性地思考，怎样吸引更多捐赠者来支持我们的事业。
女：当然可以，不过得等到下个月，因为我要去参加一个关于保护湿地的会议。
listening-text-8.summaryZh: 男士和野生动物保护协会的埃琳娜交谈，提出一个请求，埃琳娜说起近期安排。

listening-text-9.transcript:
M: Hello everyone. Welcome to our program. Today we are fortunate to have a special guest with us. Her name is Yang Liu, a performer of bamboo drifting. When did you begin to learn bamboo drifting?
W: I learned it from my grandmother when I was seven.
M: Could you share your learning experience with us?
W: With pleasure. Usually, the bamboo under my feet is about nine meters long, and the bamboo in my hands is about five meters long. I fell in the water several times when I was practicing. So keeping my body from falling into the water is the most difficult part of bamboo drifting.
M: What makes you keep going?
W: Just the love for the ancient skill. In the past 17 years, I have been drifting all year round, in winter cold and summer heat. Now I am able to do Chinese qigong on the water, and I put dance into bamboo drifting to make it elegant. As Hanfu culture has been on the rise, I started wearing Hanfu when performing, creating a beautiful feel.
M: We all know you registered on social media platforms and posted your videos.
W: Yes. I want to spread it to other countries so that more people around the world will like Chinese culture.
M: I totally agree with you. It was good to talk to you. I feel like I always learn so much more when I get the chance to speak with you about these things.
listening-text-9.translationZh:
男：大家好。欢迎收看我们的节目。今天我们很荣幸请到一位特别嘉宾。她叫杨柳，是一位独竹漂表演者。你是什么时候开始学独竹漂的？
女：我七岁时跟奶奶学的。
男：能和我们分享一下你的学艺经历吗？
女：乐意之至。通常，我脚下踩的竹子大约九米长，手里拿的竹竿大约五米长。练习的时候我掉进水里好几次。所以，不让身体掉进水里是独竹漂最难的部分。
男：是什么让你坚持下来的？
女：就是对这门古老技艺的热爱。过去 17 年里，无论冬寒还是夏热，我一年到头都在练独竹漂。现在我能在水上练中国气功，还把舞蹈融入独竹漂，让它更优美。随着汉服文化兴起，我开始穿汉服表演，营造出一种美感。
男：我们都知道你在社交媒体平台上注册了账号，发布了自己的视频。
女：是的。我想把它传播到其他国家，让世界各地更多的人喜欢中国文化。
男：我完全赞同。和你聊天很愉快。我觉得每次有机会和你聊这些事，我总能学到更多。

listening-text-10.transcript: Microplastics are everywhere in our environment. Measuring 50 to 500 micrometers in length, microplastics come from a variety of sources, including large plastics that break down into smaller pieces. Therefore, much remains unknown about the common existence of these materials within the human body, as well as their impact on human health. A research team led by Kieran Cox studied 26 papers on the amount of microplastics in common foods. Using previously reported data, the team evaluated the potential consumption of microplastics and calculated annual intake via food and drink at 34,000 to 52,000 particles. The study found that people who drink only bottled water absorb an additional 90,000 microplastics each year, compared to 4,000 among those who only drink tap water. But the food and drink that the researchers analyzed represent 15 of Americans' caloric intake. The team couldn't account for food groups like fruits, vegetables, and grains, because there simply is not enough data on their microplastic content. For those who are worried about microplastic consumption, cutting down bottled water is a good start. But as for the heart of the problem, we have to stop producing and using so much plastic.
listening-text-10.translationZh: 微塑料在我们的环境中无处不在。微塑料长 50 到 500 微米，来源多种多样，其中包括分解成小碎片的大块塑料。因此，这些物质在人体内普遍存在的情况以及它们对人体健康的影响，还有很多未知之处。由基兰·考克斯带领的研究团队研究了 26 篇关于常见食物中微塑料含量的论文。团队利用以往报告的数据，评估了人们可能摄入的微塑料量，计算出每人每年通过食物和饮料摄入 34,000 到 52,000 个微塑料颗粒。研究发现，只喝瓶装水的人每年会额外摄入 90,000 个微塑料颗粒，而只喝自来水的人只有 4,000 个。但研究人员分析的食物和饮料只占美国人热量摄入的 15%。团队无法把水果、蔬菜和谷物等食物类别算进去，因为关于它们微塑料含量的数据实在太少。对于担心摄入微塑料的人来说，少喝瓶装水是个好的开始。但要从根本上解决问题，我们必须停止生产和使用这么多塑料。

topic.subtopic: 人类生存与环境的关系

listening-text-10.summaryZh: 讲话人介绍基兰·考克斯团队关于微塑料的一项研究及其发现。

sentences.zh: 微塑料在我们的环境中无处不在。
微塑料长 50 到 500 微米，来源多种多样，其中包括分解成小碎片的大块塑料。
因此，这些物质在人体内普遍存在的情况以及它们对人体健康的影响，还有很多未知之处。
由基兰·考克斯带领的研究团队研究了 26 篇关于常见食物中微塑料含量的论文。
团队利用以往报告的数据，评估了人们可能摄入的微塑料量，计算出每人每年通过食物和饮料摄入 34,000 到 52,000 个微塑料颗粒。
研究发现，只喝瓶装水的人每年会额外摄入 90,000 个微塑料颗粒，而只喝自来水的人只有 4,000 个。
但研究人员分析的食物和饮料只占美国人热量摄入的 15%。
团队无法把水果、蔬菜和谷物等食物类别算进去，因为关于它们微塑料含量的数据实在太少。
对于担心摄入微塑料的人来说，少喝瓶装水是个好的开始。
但要从根本上解决问题，我们必须停止生产和使用这么多塑料。

evidence.quote: I'm sorry, our restaurant is not set up to take credit cards over the phone for delivery orders.

distractors.label: A

distractors.label: C
distractors.explanationZh: 餐厅（our restaurant）是接电话的男店员说的“我们餐厅”，女士是打电话来订外卖的顾客。

evidence.quote: So, as an expert, what new technology do you think we will see in 2026?

distractors.label: C
distractors.explanationZh: 技术（technology）是男士提问的话题，他请女士预测新技术，不是让她去多学技术。

evidence.quote: One in the afternoon.

question:listening:3.reasonZh: 女士问男士几点走（When will you leave?），男士答下午一点（One in the afternoon），即航班下午 1:00 起飞，选 C。

distractors.label: A
distractors.explanationZh: 上午 11 点是女士说要在机场跟他碰面的时间（see you at the airport at 11），比值机还早一点。

distractors.label: B
distractors.explanationZh: 11:20 是男士上午要办理登机手续的时间（check in at 11:20），不是起飞时间。

evidence.quote: So they need encouragement and shouldn't be made fun of.

question:listening:4.reasonZh: 女士说残疾运动员需要鼓励、不该被取笑（shouldn't be made fun of），男士完全同意（I couldn't agree more），两人都主张尊重他们，选 B。

evidence.quote: Using previously reported data, the team evaluated the potential consumption of microplastics and calculated annual intake via food and drink at 34,000 to 52,000 particles.

distractors.label: A

question:listening:18.stemTranslationZh: 基兰·考克斯的团队是怎样计算微塑料可能摄入量的？

question:listening:18.reasonZh: “分析数据”就是团队利用以往报告的数据（Using previously reported data）来估算摄入量，前一句也说他们研读了 26 篇论文（studied 26 papers），选 A。

distractors.label: C

distractors.label: B
